newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end flat, bank sector jumps.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end flat, bank sector jumps.

text.p: Swedish shares ended virtually flat on Thursday after a volatile day, with shares finally pulled off highs when Wall Street opened lower.
"Today investors are sidelined, waiting for better times," a trader said.
The Stockholm general index closed flat at 2,763.58 compared to 2,763.46 on Wednesday in turnover of 4.31 billion crowns.

Sectors were mixed with banks up 1.09 percent, lifted by merger rumours. Handelsbanken leaped 8.5 crowns to 234, while Nordbanken jumped four crowns to 269 and S-E-Banken edged 0.5 higher to 81 crowns.

Speculation about a merger between S-E-Banken and Nordbanken boosted prices as well as rumours that Dutch bank ABN Amro might bid for Nordbanken. Handelsbanken rode on positive analyst reports and hopes that the bank would benefit from others being preoccupied with mergers.
Drugs major Astra took a beating after the U.S. drug sector fell a day earlier, down 7.5 crowns to 364.5. Rival Pharmacia & Upjohn fell five to 296 crowns.
Industrivarden rose 10 to 405 after newspaper reports it and SCA would dissolve cross ownership.
The forestry sector rose 1.24 percent after non-traded forestry group Sodra said North American and Scandinavian (NorScan) pulp stocks rose by 70,000 tonnes in February.
A company spokesman said the increase was normal for the season and that it would not affect pulp prices.
SCA rose 0.5 crown to 173.5, MoDo gained four to 247.5, AssiDoman advanced 1.5 to 208.5 and Stora rose two to 109.5.
Telecoms group Ericsson gained four to 269.5 after making positive statements at a press conference in Germany.
